# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for `node_data_dir_single_writer` against input/. See
# tests/fixtures/doctor/node_data_dir_single_writer/expect.json for the NUL-byte warning, the
# canonicalisation trap and what the fcntl half of §2i's probe this fixture cannot cover.
#
# THIS CASE: NOBODY holds the data dir. The /proc tree has no monerod at all, and
# <data-dir>/lmdb/lock.mdb does not exist either -- §2i: "A missing lock.mdb means the directory was
# never opened." So `node up` may start.
# THREE DECOYS, and each one is a scan this case is designed to fail:
#   pid 1     /sbin/init splash                     -- no --data-dir
#   pid 2451  /usr/bin/monero-wallet-rpc ...        -- a MONERO binary that is not monerod
#   pid 9001  /usr/bin/monerod-not-really --data-dir /var/lib/monero
#             -- argv[0]'s BASENAME BEGINS WITH "monerod" AND IT NAMES THE VERY DATA DIR. A scan that
#             matches with starts_with("monerod"), or with a `contains` on the whole cmdline, reports
#             pid 9001 here and this case FAILS `pass` -- which is the point. The match must be on the
#             exact file name `monerod`, and §2i's own words are "a monerod whose --data-dir ...
#             resolves to the same canonical path", not "a process whose cmdline mentions it".
# status `pass`, and the detail should say so positively -- naming the data dir it checked, so a
# reader can tell a genuine all-clear from a check that looked at the wrong path. That is the failure
# mode this whole case exists for: a scan pointed at the wrong FMONERO_PROC_ROOT also reports `pass`.
# EDITED BY THE PHASE 2 DOCTOR AGENT (DESIGN.md §8 hands this directory to it): see
# decisions/phase2-doctor.md for the reason, stated case by case.
# ADDED `_probe.monerod_installed`: every check in the `node` group reports
# skip:monerod_not_installed when /usr/bin/monerod is absent, which is §4b's GREEN row for
# this machine and §7.1's "every check whose precondition is missing reports skip:<reason>".
# No file under input/ can carry that fact, so the harness states it here.
